title: Retiring an idle workspace mid-merge commits the conflict
what: prepare_retire goes from local_files straight to save_with without the unfinished() guard tidy_one uses, so a sweep over an idle workspace with a half-done merge, cherry-pick, revert or rebase commits its conflict markers as a normal save and then removes the folder.
expected: It should refuse with the same unfinished message tidy_one gives, leaving the merge and its markers for the user to resolve.

title: A damaged origin record is overwritten without being kept aside
what: load_origins turns a workspaceOrigins blob that does not parse into an empty map, and the next set_origin writes a fresh map over the key, so every madeBy and prEver record is lost with no copy kept aside and nothing shown.
expected: A blob that does not read should be kept aside the way kept::load does, and the caller told, so no record is silently destroyed.

title: A worktree Kolux did not make counts as Kolux's own
what: kolux_made accepts every worktree whose path merely has an origin record, but save_details writes such a record without madeBy, so a worktree opened from another tool and given a display name is treated as Kolux's own and the sweep may forget or retire it.
expected: Only a record that names Kolux as its maker, the madeBy check trust::made_by_kolux uses, should count, so a foreign worktree is never swept.

title: A folder inside a project never resolves to that project
what: project_known builds its containment prefix as name_key(project.path) plus a forward slash, but name_key has already turned slashes into backslashes, so on Windows the prefix never matches a child path and the folder falls through to the Git lookup.
expected: A path under the project's folder should resolve to that project, using the separator name_key itself produces.

title: A double-star ignore stops hiding folders below the top level
what: rules_of rewrites a pattern with replace("**/", ""), so `**/build` becomes `build`; the rule stays anchored and only a top-level build matches, while a nested a/build is scanned and repositories inside it are found.
expected: `**/build` should hide a build folder at any depth, as Git does, so nothing under it is scanned.

title: A failed forget leaves the workspace's records half wiped
what: forget_workspace clears the admin record, typed name, parent, opened time, board status and origin as separate writes; when a later write fails the call returns Err but the earlier records are already gone, so a retry or a new worktree at that path inherits a half-forgotten state.
expected: The records should go in one all-or-nothing write, or in an order that leaves nothing lost, so a failed forget changes nothing.

title: A drive-relative workspaces folder escapes the project root
what: set_place saves any folder that is not is_absolute() as if it were project-relative, but on Windows `C:ws` is drive-relative and Path::join replaces the whole base with it, so the workspaces land outside the project the setting promised.
expected: A saved folder that is not fully absolute should be joined safely, by refusing it or treating it as relative, so it can never leave the project root.

title: A project's relative workspaces folder is never swept for trash
what: trash_folders turns each project's saved workspaces folder straight into a PathBuf, but that value is stored verbatim and resolved from the project root when worktrees are made, so with a relative folder such as `ws` the sweep looks in the app's own directory and the real trash is never cleared.
expected: A relative per-project folder should be joined to the project path the same way place_root does, so the sweep looks where the worktrees are.
